mechanism: Run a non-trading screenshot EA in Strategy Tester visual mode so dynamic (history-redrawing) channel indicators are forced to recompute tick-by-tick. Compare Barishpolets Moving Channels (extrema-anchored) against a mean-price equidistant two-channel stack (weekly + ~33-hour). Flag regime instability when nearby extrema make the tested channel flip ~±45° across successive bars while the mean-price channel stays coherent; use that flip rate as a quality/regime-reliability sensor before trusting channel borders.
data_needed: OHLC history for symbol/period under test; indicator buffers for extrema-based channel and mean-price channel; optional WindowScreenShot sequence keyed by ScreenShotStart/Step/Max.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M30; example window 4–7 Dec 2007; weekly vs 33-hour channel overlay
why_new_for_mis: Treats redraw/flip of dynamic channels as an observable regime-quality signal (stable vs thrashing geometry) rather than only as a backtest artifact—MIS can score channel sensors for live trust.
quote: two extremums, through which one of the channel lines should be drawn, are located close to each other. In such cases, some indicators start "throw" the channel from 45 degrees downside to 45 degrees upside, and then back

mechanism: For each bar i define reachability paths P(t) (max excursion) and L(t) (adverse excursion). With fixed TP/SL, record tP and tL; success iff tP<tL (buy). Build constant set M1 of all bars satisfying tP<tL for the symbol. Build M2 from any indicator/candlestick signal set. Trade quality = |M1∩M2| vs false hits in M2\M1. Analysis runs from successful price outcomes back to indicator readings, not from discrete semaphore signals forward.
data_needed: Full OHLC history (≥~100k bars preferred); fixed TP/SL in points; indicator or pattern boolean series for M2; IndoExpert-style bar labels of profit/loss.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD, EURUSD, GBPJPY; H1 and M15 for hammer study; method is TF-agnostic
why_new_for_mis: Flips MIS feature discovery: lock a TP/SL outcome geometry first, then mine which continuous indicator states co-occur—avoids information loss from early signal discretization.
quote: market analysis should not be performed from indicator signals to price prediction, but from the right price to indicator readings collection.

mechanism: At each bar i build an N-MA fan (article: 40 MAs, step 3 periods). Scan prior history for visually/numerically identical fans; for each twin, grid TP/SL (e.g. 20..120 pts) and tally nTP, nSL, total Profit, Expected payoff=nTP/(nTP+nSL). Keep configurations with Fans>10, Expected payoff>80%, Profit>0; use that empirical expectancy as the live entry score for the current fan geometry.
data_needed: Long OHLC series (article: GBPUSD M5, 125000 bars / ~434 days); N MA periods; TP/SL grid; twin-match tolerance on fan shape.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD M5 (125k bars); also method discussed with H1/M15 FX pairs
why_new_for_mis: Uses multi-MA fan geometry as a reusable regime fingerprint whose live signal is historical twin expectancy—not a single MA cross—giving MIS a nonparametric pattern-match sensor.
quote: For each bar i we settle a fan consisting of N moving averages. Going through the history from beginning to the bar investigated we find identical fans and save their bars' numbers.

mechanism: Detect hammer (body in upper part of bar; short/absent upper shadow; lower shadow ≥2× body) in a downtrend (e.g. MA5 slope). After each hit, record max/min over next Z bars and map probability of hitting grids of TakeProfit N vs StopLoss L (priority search adverse then favorable for buys). Prefer TP/SL pairs with positive expected path; article found H1 response weak (downtrend often continues) while M15 GBPUSD liked TP≈150 / SL≈65.
data_needed: OHLC; hammer geometry ratios; prior bars for downtrend context; forward Z-bar extrema; TP/SL grid sweeps.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD, EURUSD, GBPJPY; H1 and M15
why_new_for_mis: Turns a classic candlestick reversal label into a measured forward-path / TP-SL actuation sensor with pair- and TF-specific validity—usable as a change-event prior for MIS.

mechanism: State machine UpZ with TempMax/TempMin (and bar indices in forward numbering). On up-segment SwitchLevel=TempMax−H·Point; if Low breaks SwitchLevel, fix CurMax and flip to down (symmetric for minima). Work completed bars only so live state matches history. SwitchLevel() is the pluggable slowing definition (fixed H, channel bound, etc.).
data_needed: OHLC High/Low series; threshold H (or alternate SwitchLevel rule); MinBars; state vars UpZ, TempMax/Min, CurMax/Min.
